name: Rome
hook: Founding twins, emperors and a road that still runs: the Roman facts Jeopardy keeps asking.

facts.label: Romulus and Remus
facts.statement: Rome's founding myth makes the twins Romulus and Remus sons of Mars, set adrift on the Tiber and suckled by a she-wolf.

facts.label: the Tiber
facts.statement: The Tiber runs through Rome; it flooded so badly in 1598 that the Pantheon stood in 12 feet of water.

facts.label: the Punic Wars
facts.statement: Rome fought Carthage in three Punic Wars — the name comes from Latin for "Phoenician" — and destroyed Carthage in 146 B.C.

facts.label: Nero
facts.statement: Nero built the Domus Aurea, or Golden House, after the Great Fire of 64; the fiddle story is legend.

facts.label: the Appian Way
facts.statement: The Appian Way was antiquity's "Queen of Roads," stretching from Rome southeast to Brindisi on the Adriatic.

facts.label: the Colosseum
facts.statement: The Colosseum was begun by Emperor Vespasian; a 1590 papal plan would have turned it into a wool factory.

facts.label: Julius Caesar
facts.statement: Julius Caesar made himself dictator for life after beating Pompey; Rome's coins marked his murder with daggers and the Ides of March.
